data.title: Push
data.tagline: Upload local commits to a remote repository
data.description: Push sends commits and branch references to a remote such as GitHub. It shares committed history, not uncommitted files. The remote may reject the push if new work exists there or if branch rules require review.

use: Back up committed work to the remote
avoid: Expect uncommitted changes to be uploaded
Force-push a shared branch without coordination
Push secrets and try to delete them later
Ignore a rejection without checking remote changes

lessonPractice.title: After a local fix commit, how do you safely share it with remote collaborators?

options.label: Inspect the commit and target branch, push to its remote branch, then confirm the remote hash
options.feedback: Correct. Push writes shared remote state, so confirm scope and target, then verify the result.

options.label: Force-push straight to main so remote exactly matches local
options.feedback: A force push can overwrite other people’s remote history.

options.label: Send edited files to a teammate; Git history need not be shared
options.feedback: A file copy loses traceable commit relationships and does not update the shared branch.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect the current branch, commits to push, and its upstream. Once it contains only this fix, push to that branch. Report the remote branch and latest commit hash; do not rewrite main or use force.
